title: `to_uppercase`, `to_lowercase`: Rust's Unicode mappings
description: Case mapping is Rust's `str::to_uppercase` and `to_lowercase`: full Unicode mappings, which can change the length (`ß` is `SS`, `İ` lowercases to `i̇`), with a final sigma (`ΣΑΣ` lowercases to `σας`). On ASCII they agree with the reference on every probe row.
reference: `upper`, `lower` with `char_set: UTF8`, a black box defined as Rust's `str::to_uppercase` (`Text.upper`); Lean evaluates them on ASCII only.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
